name: app-6ab6ad64a36881919b779453ee18bb6b
description: Turn a rough resume into a finished one without leaving the chat.

interface.longDescription: Turn a rough resume into a finished one without leaving the chat. Paste your resume or upload it, and the app scores it the way applicant tracking systems read it: a deterministic score out of 100, a letter grade, the score by area (structure, content, contact details, job tailoring), the issues to fix first and, when you add a job posting, which of its keywords your resume already covers and which are missing. ChatGPT then helps you improve the wording using only your real experience, re-scores the new version, and when the resume is complete opens it in the ResumeNext editor with everything already loaded: every role, bullet and contact detail, plus the target role, company and job description you gave. In the editor you can keep editing, switch between templates, follow the live ATS score and finish the document. The link is private and valid for seven days. Nothing is stored until you ask for the editor link, and the resume text is used only to analyze it and to open it in the editor.
defaultPrompt: Review my resume and give me an ATS score
Tailor my resume to this job posting
Open my resume in an editor so I can pick a template

positive.description: Resume review with a real ATS score. The app must call analyze_resume with the complete pasted text and answer with the returned score, grade, weakest area and the first fixes, without inventing a number. Attach the sample resume to the message: https://resumenext.io/samples/alex-morgan-resume.txt
positive.prompt: Review the attached resume and give me an ATS score.
positive.expected_behavior: The reply quotes the score out of 100 and the letter grade returned by the tool, names the weakest area, lists the fixes to make first (for example expanding the summary and adding more detail), and offers to improve the resume or open it in the editor. No editor link yet.

positive.description: Keyword coverage against a job posting. The app must call analyze_resume with the resume and the job description and report matched and missing keywords from the tool result. Attach the sample resume to the message: https://resumenext.io/samples/alex-morgan-resume.txt
positive.prompt: Here is a job posting: Senior Backend Engineer. Requirements: Python, Go, Kubernetes, Terraform, gRPC, PostgreSQL, observability, 5+ years of experience. Which of its keywords does the attached resume cover and which are missing?
positive.expected_behavior: The reply states the job-tailored score and the keyword coverage percentage from the tool, lists matched keywords (Python, Go, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL) and missing ones (Terraform, gRPC, observability), and suggests where the missing ones could honestly fit.

positive.description: Improve, then re-score. The app rewrites the resume in the chat using only the supplied facts and calls analyze_resume again on the rewritten version so the user sees the new score. Attach the sample resume to the message: https://resumenext.io/samples/alex-morgan-resume.txt
positive.prompt: Improve the wording of the attached resume for a backend engineering role and tell me the new ATS score.
positive.expected_behavior: The reply shows the rewritten resume (same facts, stronger wording, no invented employers, dates or metrics) followed by the new score and grade returned by analyze_resume on that rewritten text.

positive.description: Open the finished resume in the editor. The app must call prepare_resume_editor with the complete resume text, show the inline card (score and 'Open in the ResumeNext editor' button) and give the link in text; opening the link shows the builder with the resume loaded, no login required. Attach the sample resume to the message: https://resumenext.io/samples/alex-morgan-resume.txt
positive.prompt: Open the attached resume in an editor so I can pick a template.
positive.expected_behavior: The card shows the score and the button; the reply also contains the https://resumenext.io/builder?session=... link and says the editor opens with the resume already loaded, with templates and a live ATS score. Opening the link in a browser shows the builder with Alex Morgan's resume filled in and its ATS score, without a login step.

positive.description: Tailor to a job and hand off with the job context. The app must call prepare_resume_editor with the complete final resume plus target role, company and job description, so the editor opens in job-tailored mode. Attach the sample resume to the message: https://resumenext.io/samples/alex-morgan-resume.txt
positive.prompt: Tailor the attached resume for the Senior Backend Engineer role at Stripe (requirements: Python, Go, Kubernetes, Terraform, gRPC, PostgreSQL, observability) and open the result in the ResumeNext editor.
positive.expected_behavior: The reply shows the tailored resume (Terraform, gRPC and observability named as gaps, not added as skills), then the card and the editor link; the card badge reads 'Tailored to the job' and the editor opens with the resume, the target role Senior Backend Engineer, the company Stripe and the job description already set.

negative.description: General knowledge question, unrelated to resumes: the app must not be invoked.
negative.prompt: What is the capital of Portugal?
negative.expected_behavior: ChatGPT answers directly (Lisbon) without calling any ResumeNext tool.

negative.description: Creative request outside the app's purpose: no tool call.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about autumn in Milan.
negative.expected_behavior: ChatGPT writes the poem itself; no ResumeNext tool is called.

negative.description: Job search, which the app does not do: no tool call and no invented capability.
negative.prompt: Find me open backend engineering jobs in Berlin posted this week.
negative.expected_behavior: ChatGPT does not call any ResumeNext tool; it answers with its own capabilities and does not claim the app can search jobs.

publication.release_notes: Developer name update only: the developer name shown becomes ResumeNext, the product name. No change to the tools, the server or the listing text.
